title: Avoid z-index Whenever Possible
brief: A 2020 article by Daniel Rotter arguing for CSS layouts that avoid z-index. The thesis is in the URL slug; the article's quality is unverified.
caveat: The thesis is in the URL slug; the article's quality is unverified.
details: This 2020 article by Daniel Rotter argues that CSS z-index is the billion-dollar mistake of web development and should be avoided whenever possible. It walks through why escalating z-index values don't scale, explains stacking contexts (why a higher z-index can still lose inside a parent's stacking context), and shows how component-based frameworks like React make the problem worse. The practical remedy: order elements correctly in the DOM so later elements paint on top, and use techniques like flex-direction column-reverse instead of z-index for sticky headers.
